newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, export ideas boost nearbys.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, export ideas boost nearbys.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed, with nearby months boosted late by commercial buying which again stirred talk that U.S. wheat export sales to Egypt and probably Pakistan were being covered, traders said.

Egypt this week bought U.S. wheat and there were rumblings that Egypt this weekend would be in the market for another one half to one million tonnes of wheat. Pakistan is slated in the market next week for one-half million tonnes of wheat, and the U.S. should land a large portion of that business.

Continental Grain bought five million bushels of September and was said buying two million bushels of September in the Kansas City market. Cargill Investor Services bought three million September, FIMAT Futures bought three million September and sold five million September and 2.5 million December, traders said.
Gains in wheat were limited by signals the market was overbought for the near term after the strong rally early this week.
CBOT wheat futures closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher to four lower, with September up 1-3/4 at $3.58-1/2.
A low number in USDA's weekly export sales report also trimmed advances in wheat futures, the traders said.
"Wheat and corn sales were atrocious," a trader said.
USDA said Thursday that U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended July 17 totalled 259,500 tonnes, below expectations for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Spread trading was light with Produce Grain doing one-half million bushels of December/September at 13 cents, premium December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000 contracts, below the 34,410 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, Term Commodities bought 400 September $3.50 puts at eight to 8-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 400 September $3.90 puts and bought 400 December $3.90 puts at three cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, below the 13,803 traded Wednesday.
